---
title: "The tables"
---

```{r}
#| label: load
library(data.table)
tags <- as.data.table(read.csv("../tags/tags_auto.csv", check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
dict <- as.data.table(read.csv("../dictionary/dictionary_auto.csv", check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
val  <- as.data.table(read.csv("../validate/report.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
meta <- rbindlist(lapply(list.files("../output", "__dataset.json$", full.names = TRUE), function(f) {
  j <- jsonlite::read_json(f)
  data.table(table = j$table, title = j$title, citation = j$citation,
             licence = j$intellectualRights$spdx, sourceURL = j$sourceURL,
             protocol = j$samplingProtocol, coverage = j$temporalCoverage,
             columns = paste(unlist(j$columns), collapse = ", "),
             coarsened = isTRUE(j$coordinatesCoarsened$value))
}))
d <- merge(merge(tags, dict[, .(table, description)], by = "table"), meta, by = "table")
d <- merge(d, val[, .(table, irw_v1, irw_warnings)], by = "table")
setorder(d, table)
redivis <- "https://redivis.com/datasets/4j5q"
gh <- "https://github.com/ben-domingue/eco/blob/main"
```

Every table below was built by a script in the repository's `data/`
directory from a public deposit, validated against the draft standard and
against the IRW v1.0 validator, and published on Redivis as the dataset
[`datapages.eco`](`r redivis`). Each table ships with a `__taxa`
side table (taxon resolution via GBIF, plus traits where the source has them)
and, where there are primary periods, a `__periods` side table, and carries a
`__dataset.json` with the EML and Darwin Core fields the standard borrows.

Tables marked **hold** fall below the proposed sample floor of 30 units and
would not be published under the current draft. They are kept because they
exercise the rules, and because the floor is itself an open decision.

## Summary

```{r}
#| label: summary
#| output: asis
d[, dims := sprintf("%s × %s × %s × %s", n_units, n_taxa, n_periods, n_occasions)]
d[, state := ifelse(grepl("hold", status), "hold", "ok")]
d[, name := sprintf("[`%s`](#%s)", table, table)]
out <- d[, .(Table = name, Family = model_family, Taxa = taxon_group,
             Protocol = sampling_protocol, `Units × taxa × periods × occasions` = dims,
             Rows = format(n_rows, big.mark = ","), Licence = licence, Status = state)]
cat(knitr::kable(out, format = "pipe"), sep = "\n")
```

The four dimensions are counts of distinct `unit`, `taxon`, `period` and
`occasion` values. The row count is the number of survey observations, which
is smaller than the product of the four whenever some unit-occasion
combinations were not surveyed.

## Each table

```{r}
#| label: cards
#| output: asis
for (i in seq_len(nrow(d))) {
  r <- d[i]
  cat(sprintf("\n### `%s` {#%s}\n\n", r$table, r$table))
  cat(sprintf("**%s**\n\n", r$title))
  cat(sprintf("%s\n\n", r$description))
  cat("| | |\n|---|---|\n")
  cat(sprintf("| Family | %s |\n", r$model_family))
  cat(sprintf("| Design | %s |\n", r$design))
  cat(sprintf("| Protocol | %s |\n", r$protocol))
  cat(sprintf("| Response | `%s` |\n", r$response_type))
  cat(sprintf("| Coverage | %s; %s; %s |\n", r$country, r$realm, r$coverage))
  cat(sprintf("| Coordinates | %s |\n", r$coordinates))
  cat(sprintf("| Size | %s units, %s taxa, %s periods, %s occasions, %s rows |\n",
              r$n_units, r$n_taxa, r$n_periods, r$n_occasions, format(r$n_rows, big.mark = ",")))
  cat(sprintf("| Sample floor | %s |\n", r$sample_floor))
  cat(sprintf("| Validation | draft validator passes; IRW v1.0 %s%s |\n", r$irw_v1,
              if (nzchar(r$irw_warnings)) sprintf(" (warnings: %s)", r$irw_warnings) else ""))
  cat(sprintf("| Columns | %s |\n", paste0("`", strsplit(r$columns, ", ")[[1]], "`", collapse = " ")))
  cat(sprintf("| Source | [%s](%s), %s |\n", r$sourceURL, r$sourceURL, r$licence))
  cat(sprintf("| Script | [`data/%s.R`](%s/data/%s.R) |\n", r$table, gh, r$table))
  cat(sprintf("| Status | %s |\n", r$status))
  if (nzchar(r$notes)) cat(sprintf("\nNotes: %s\n", r$notes))
  cat(sprintf("\nCitation: %s\n", r$citation))
}
```

## Getting the data

The dataset is on Redivis as [`datapages.eco`](`r redivis`), with a free
Redivis account. The tables there are the first published version; the
standard is still a draft, so names and columns may change between versions.
The CSVs in the repository's `output/` directory are the same files and can
be read directly; rebuild them from source with

```sh
Rscript data/run_all.R && Rscript validate/validate_all.R
```

from the repository root. The scripts cache downloads and are deterministic,
with assertions on facts about each source so that a changed deposit fails
loudly.
